title: Fairplay Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Fairplay wells have a 170 ft median depth, 8 gpm median yield, and estimated finished costs of $17,000-$29,000.
h1: Fairplay, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost Guide
intro_html:
Buying land or a home near Fairplay means looking closely at the well record, not just the view or the road access. Within 5 miles of Fairplay, Colorado, DWR records list 2,178 permitted wells. Of those, 1,410 are recorded as constructed, 1,504 report a total depth, 1,000 report a pump yield, and 209 report a static water level.

The local pattern is mountain bedrock. Most permits name an unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer, so nearby records are useful for setting expectations but cannot guarantee what a new hole will produce. Use the information below to compare a property with the surrounding area and to build a realistic investigation and construction budget.

sections.heading: Fairplay well depth and the mountain ground below
sections.html:
The median recorded well depth around Fairplay is 170 feet. The middle half runs from 120 to 220 feet, meaning many ordinary bids should fall in that range, although the spread is wide. The 90th percentile is 300 feet, and the deepest well on record reaches 752 feet.

Depth mix gives a practical picture: 14% of wells are under 100 feet, 75% are between 100 and 300 feet, and 11% are between 300 and 600 feet. No recorded wells fall in the 600-plus-foot category. These are fractured mountain formations, mainly granite and gneiss. A driller may need to keep going when a shallow fracture does not provide enough water, so a bid should explain the per-foot rate and what happens if the target depth is exceeded.

sections.heading: What Fairplay wells produce
sections.html:
Among the 1,000 wells reporting a pump yield, the median is 8.0 gallons per minute. The middle half produces 5.0 to 11.0 gallons per minute. That is a workable range for many domestic homes, but a pump test and storage design still matter because reported yield is not the same as unlimited daily supply.

The local records show 0% under 1 gallon per minute, 11% from 1 to 5 gallons per minute, 74% from 5 to 15 gallons per minute, and 15% above 15 gallons per minute. A buyer should not treat the median as a promise for a specific lot. Ask for the well construction report, pumping information, and any water-quality results. Household-use exempt wells are generally subject to Colorado's 35-gallon-per-minute pumping limit, along with the limits written on the permit.

sections.heading: Water levels around Fairplay and what the record suggests
sections.html:
The median reported static water level is 90 feet below the surface, with the middle half from 58 to 130 feet. That measurement is the depth to water while the well is at rest, not the level during pumping. Pump placement, pressure-tank settings, and available storage should be designed from the actual well report rather than the area median.

The decade figures show a change in the available measurements: the median was 80 feet below surface in the 2010s and 100 feet in the 2020s. That is a deeper reported water level in the newer decade, but only 209 wells report static water levels, and the records do not establish a cause or prove a uniform decline across Fairplay. Have the well tested under pumping conditions before relying on it for a new home.

sections.heading: Fairplay permit history and the drillers in the record
sections.html:
Fairplay has a long permit history. Records show 2 permits in the 1950s, 9 in the 1960s, 171 in the 1970s, 242 in the 1980s, 590 in the 1990s, 558 in the 2000s, 217 in the 2010s, and 201 in the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025. Domestic or household use accounts for 90% of the listed use mix; stock is 4%, irrigation is 0%, and monitoring is 6%.

Allen Drilling & Excavating Co., Inc. (Allen, Jack R.) appears most often, with 757 records. Whitewater Drilling Inc (Benkufski, John D.) appears on 157, and Five Star Inc. (Werner, Peter S.) on 153. These records show who has worked in the area, not who is available or best for a particular lot. Confirm current licensing, insurance, scheduling, and the exact scope of a written proposal.

sections.heading: A Fairplay well drilling budget
sections.html:
For fractured mountain bedrock around Fairplay, the drilling model uses a typical rate of $65 to $100 per foot. At the 170-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $11,000 to $17,000. That is only the hole. A finished system with a pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at about $17,000 to $29,000.

Actual bids can change with access, casing and grout requirements, terrain, pump depth, power availability, and the amount of rock excavation needed for utilities. Ask whether the proposal includes mobilization, drilling, casing, grout, development, testing, pump equipment, electrical work, trenching, and permits. A low per-foot quote may not be the low installed price if several of those items are separate.

sections.heading: Risks to check before building near Fairplay
sections.html:
Fractured granite and gneiss can be unpredictable. A neighboring well may be deep and productive while a nearby hole finds a different fracture pattern. The records show 8 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 840 historic mine features, and 4 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites within about 10 miles. Those mapped sites do not prove contamination at a particular parcel, but they justify a site-specific water test and a review of mining and environmental history.

Low yield, a dry hole, poor casing or grout, and inadequate pump testing are separate concerns. Confirm the well permit and construction report with Colorado DWR. Check septic setbacks, soil and slope conditions, driveway access, utility trench routes, and the intended household use before closing. In an over-appropriated basin, an augmentation plan may be needed for some new uses; the permit and county or water-court requirements control.

sections.heading: Buying or building on a Fairplay lot
sections.html:
Start with the exact parcel, then compare its well record with records near Alma, Como, Jefferson, Blue River, Leadville, and Leadville North. Those nearby areas can provide useful local context, but Fairplay's fractured-bedrock conditions make the immediate neighbors more valuable than a broad regional average.

For an existing home, obtain the permit, construction report, pump information, water-quality results, and maintenance history. Have the well flow and pressure tested, and verify that the septic system matches the permitted use. For vacant land, get a driller's site review and a written drilling budget before treating the parcel as buildable. Confirm access for a rig, room for the well and septic system, electrical service, and the water right or permit conditions that apply to the planned home.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Fairplay, Colorado?
faq.a: The median recorded well depth within 5 miles of Fairplay is 170 feet. The middle half runs from 120 to 220 feet. About 75% are between 100 and 300 feet, while the deepest recorded well is 752 feet. Fractured granite and gneiss make the actual depth for a parcel uncertain, so nearby well reports are useful but not a guarantee.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Fairplay?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $65 to $100 per foot in fractured mountain bedrock. At the 170-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at about $11,000 to $17,000. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at about $17,000 to $29,000. Access, casing, grout, power, and terrain can change the bid.

faq.q: How much water do Fairplay wells produce?
faq.a: Among 1,000 wells reporting pump yield, the median is 8.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 5.0 to 11.0 gallons per minute. Records show 74% producing 5 to 15 gallons per minute and 0% under 1 gallon per minute. A buyer should still require a pump test because fractured bedrock varies from lot to lot.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Fairplay?
faq.a: The area records identify 8 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 840 historic mine features, and 4 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites within about 10 miles. That does not establish a problem at every property. Test the actual well for common minerals, bacteria, and site-specific concerns, and review the result with a qualified laboratory or water professional before drinking it.

faq.q: Is Fairplay a good place to build a home on a well?
faq.a: It can be, but the parcel needs a well and septic review before purchase. Most local permits are for domestic or household use, and the median yield is 8.0 gallons per minute. Confirm the permit, water right conditions, access, power, septic suitability, and drilling budget. Colorado's 35-gallon-per-minute exempt-well pumping limit and any augmentation requirements may affect planned use.
